title: Choose the landing-page composition
question: Which structure should guide the AssistDesk landing-page redesign? Keep its content truthful and its existing sign-in and registration flow intact.

options.label: Campus Wayfinding Board
options.thesis: A request begins with a clear route to the right support team.
options.viewport: The headline and start action lead into a connected service route, with the campus support teams mapped as destinations.
options.risk: The wayfinding diagram must stay subordinate to the real action and readable content.

options.label: The Fold-out Service Sheet
options.lineage: Campus service leaflets and unfolding reference sheets
options.thesis: One clear sheet opens into the steps and services behind a support request.
options.viewport: A single continuous sheet moves from the support offer to request steps and department help without becoming a row of feature cards.
options.risk: The fold metaphor can feel decorative unless every panel clarifies a real step.

options.label: Campus Service Window
options.lineage: A campus help counter and its numbered service slips
options.thesis: The visitor sees where to begin and what follow-up looks like before signing in.
options.viewport: A campus service window frames a clear request action, while a single receipt shows the real submit-track-update flow.
options.risk: A counter scene must remain a working webpage, not an illustration of a webpage.
